title: Tasheel Finance enters first revolving securitization agreement with Citi and Sixth Street, valued at $588mln
summary: It marks the first securitization transaction undertaken by the Company
thbAction: Map the news to THB's provider CRM for referral growth, patient lifecycle engagement, and multi-facility relationship management across hospital and provider networks.
contentHtml:
Mohammed Galal, Managing Director of United International Holding Company. Image Courtesy: United International Holding Company

It marks the first securitization transaction undertaken by the Company

Press Release

United International Holding Company (Tasheel) announces that its subsidiary, United Company for Financial Services (Tasheel Finance), has entered into a revolving securitization agreement with Citi and Sixth Street on 24th November 2026, with a total value of USD 588 million (SAR 2.2 billion) over a three-year period.

The agreement represents a strategic milestone in the Company's journey, as it marks the first securitization transaction undertaken by the Company. It reflects the quality of its financing portfolio and the efficiency of its management, including the quality of its customer base and the effectiveness of its portfolio risk management practices. The transaction also represents an important development in diversifying the Company's funding sources and enhancing its financial flexibility, supporting its ability to sustain growth and expand its business. It is also aimed at attracting foreign investments to the Saudi financial market, in line with Saudi Vision 2030.

The transaction has been structured so that the transferred receivables will be derecognized from the consolidated financial statements. A receivables portfolio of approximately USD 186 million (approx. SAR 699 million) is expected to be securitized during 2026, with the remaining amounts to be drawn down in phases in accordance with the terms of the agreement and during its validity period.

The proceeds generated from this transaction will primarily be used to repay part of the Company's existing debt, while also supporting its future growth strategies.

The securitization of part of the receivables portfolio is expected to have a positive impact on the Company's profitability in 2026, estimated at approximately SAR 108 million, which will enable the Company to continue supporting customer-related provisions in line with its strategy.

Commenting on the transaction, Mohammed Galal, Managing Director of United International Holding Company, said 

“This transaction is a strategic milestone for Tasheel, reflecting the progress we have made in developing our financing business and strengthening our financial capabilities. By diversifying our funding sources and enhancing our financial flexibility, we are better positioned to expand our financing portfolio and serve more customers as we move into our next phase of growth.”

Luay Mahasneh, Head of Private Markets, Middle East and Africa at Citi, commented:

“Tasheel Finance's inaugural securitization marks an important milestone in the company's evolution and reflects the strength of its financing platform. Citi is proud to support Tasheel Finance in diversifying its funding sources and enhancing its financial flexibility, helping create a scalable foundation for future growth. Transactions such as this contribute to the continued development and sophistication of Saudi Arabia's capital markets”

Ahmed Ismail, Managing Director and Head of Middle East at Sixth Street, commented:

“Tasheel has built a strong consumer financing business, and this transaction gives the company greater capacity to pursue its growth ambitions and serve more customers. Sixth Street is proud to support Tasheel’s long-term objectives and participate in Saudi Arabia’s growing capital markets role in connecting international investment with the region’s financing needs” 

About United International Holding Company (Tasheel)

United International Holding Company (Tasheel) is a Saudi-based financial services holding company, headquartered in Al Khobar and listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul). It is the parent company of United Company for Financial Services (Tasheel Finance), a Saudi Central Bank–regulated provider of Sharia-compliant consumer finance, including personal finance and credit cards, delivered through digital-first processes. Established in 2019, Tasheel Finance has a loan book of SAR 3.2 billion. The Company reported revenues of SAR 616 million for the first nine months of 2026.
